caseno: Criminal Appeal No. 727 of 1974 with Jail Appeal No. 28 of 1976.
lawyer:
Mujibur Rahman with Faruque Ahmed ----- For Appellant (Appeal No.727/74). 
Sajjadul Huq ----- For the State.
parties:
S. M. Farooque alias Syed Farooque ----- Appellant.
Vs.
The State ----- Respondent.
full_judgment: 7. Mr. Mujibur Rahman, learned Advocate for the appellant, Faruque, has contended that the first, information Report, Ext. I, is not the one filed first in point of time and that in the original First Information Report the complainant did not mention the name of any dacoit recognised but after arrest of the accused on suspicion on the following day the original First Information Report was replaced by a new one, Ext. 1 bringing in the story of direct recognition. In support of this contention he got the General Diary brought from the police station and referred to certain, Entries therein. Entry No. 414 of the General Diary contains the substance of the First Information Report Ext. 1 and this First Information Report shows that the miscreants were recognised by name. This Entry is shown to have been made at 11-45 P.M. of 15.6.73. But the subsequent Entries Nos. 415-419 are found over-written showing replacements of figures such as, No. 414 was changed into No. 415, No. 415 was changed into No. 416; No. 416 changed into No. 417; No. 417 changed into No. 418 and No. 418 changed into No. 419. Secondly, the impugned Entry No. 414 spread over 8 lines were compressed into a space (at the bottom of the page) which can hardly accommodate two lines. Some words of this Entry are also found over-written. From these things Mr. Mujibur Rahman contended that Entry No. 413 was the last Entry in the General Diary for the day, 15.6.73 and the next chronological Entry No. 414 in respect of a different matter was made at 00-10 of the following day, 16.6.73; but when the impugned First Information Report, lodged in the morning of 16-6-73 was sought to be accommodated, its substance was inserted below Entry No. 413 and given Entry No. 414 and consequently all the subsequent Entries Nos. were increased by over-writing. These Entries including the impugned Entry No. 414 were made by an Asstt. S. I. of Police, A. Malek who also received the First Information Report (Ext. 1) and filled the First Information Report Form. But Mr. Malek has not been examined in this case nor has any reason been given for his exclusion. Again, the First Information Report shows that it was dispatched to the court, 1/2 a mile off, at 8-30 am, of 16.6.73. But the endorsement of the S.D.O. thereupon shows that it was received by him on 20.6.73. His Order-Sheet shows that the case-file started in his office on 17.6.73 when the accused were produced before him as to the telephonic message of the complainant which preceded his written First Information Report it got no mention in the General Diary. These facts and circumstances tend to support the defence contentions that the impugned First Information Report was not lodged at the relevant night that the telephonic message and one written ejahar first received from the complainant. did not contain the story of recognition of any robber and that is why probably, these matters were not entered in the General Diary during the night, but when the impugned First Infer- matron Report was lodged after arrest of the accused, this matter was entered post-dated by inserting the impugned Entry below Entry No. 413 and. above the original Entry No. 414 which was then changed into Entry No. 415, by over-writing. Malek who made these Entries and received the telephonic message is found to have been purposely withheld. Under section 114(g) of the Evidence Act, we, having regard to these circumstances, draw a presumption that had. Mr. Malek been examined as a witness he would not have supported the prosecution case as to the time of filing of the impugned First Information Report. It may be mentioned here that during the trial the defence made an application to the learned Magistrate to call for the General Diary in order to check up the relevant Entries but the learned Magistrate did not allow it.
